preconditions.description: The number of vertices n is between 2 and 300,000 inclusive.
There are exactly n-1 edges describing the broom structure.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(u, int) and isinstance(v, int) and isinstance(x, str) and len(x) == 1 and x.islower() for u, v, x in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge consists of two integer vertices and a single lowercase Latin letter.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n for u, v, _ in edges)
preconditions.description: All vertex indices are within the range [1, n].
Vertex 1 is the root of the broom.

postconditions.expression: min_broom_size == min(broom_size_after_simplification(p) for p in valid_p_values)
postconditions.description: The first output line is the minimum possible size of the broom achievable by choosing an optimal p.

postconditions.expression: p_output == min(p for p in valid_p_values if broom_size_after_simplification(p) == min_broom_size)
postconditions.description: The second output line is the smallest integer p that achieves the minimum broom size.

postconditions.expression: valid_p_values == [p for p in range(1, max_word_length + 1) if exists_word_of_length_at_least_p(p)]
postconditions.description: The set of valid p values includes all integers from 1 to the maximum word length where at least one word has length >= p.
The broom size for a given p is the number of vertices in the tree formed by the simplified words (where the p-th character is removed from all words of length >= p).
